pages.quiz:
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — 100 °C

2. A — Glucose and oxygen

3. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

7. D — Ice melting to water

8. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

9. A — newton (N)

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

12. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
